meta.label: Airlines
meta.attribution: Reliability and cancellation scores come only from the UK Civil Aviation Authority's own 2025 annual punctuality tables (the 2025 On Time Performance Tables workbook, Top 50 airlines sheet, run 10 March 2026). The CAA ranks that sheet's 50 airlines by the number of flights operated in the period, at the UK airports it reports on, which number 25 in the same workbook. The reliability score is the share of flights the CAA records as on time, meaning within 15 minutes of schedule, with arrivals and departures counted together; the cancellation score is 100 minus the share of the airline's total flights the CAA records as cancelled, so a higher cancellation score means fewer cancelled flights, not a better on-time record. The CAA defines a cancelled flight as the non-operation of a previously planned flight, announced less than 24 hours before or after its scheduled departure time, and its Total Flights count includes operated, cancelled and unmatched flights. These figures describe flights to and from the UK specifically, not an airline's worldwide network, and a carrier can perform differently on routes the CAA does not cover. A search of the same table on 2026-09-29 found no row for Southwest, which is not among the 50 airlines listed, so it carries no reliability or cancellation score here rather than a guessed one. Cost scores describe only the fee an airline itself publishes for a first and second checked bag on a standard fare, taken from the airline's own fee page or from a news outlet's direct report of the airline's own announcement; the score is this catalogue's own translation of that published fee, and the surrounding fare rules, into a comparable number, not an official ranking, and it says nothing about the base fare itself, which changes by route, season and how far ahead someone books. Where neither an airline's own fee page nor a direct report of its own announcement could be read, the cost cell is left blank rather than filled with a guess. The differences in emissions between two airlines flying the same route are real but small next to the choice to fly at all: Our World in Data's own analysis of UK government transport emissions factors finds that taking a train instead of a domestic flight cuts emissions by around 86 percent, a bigger swing than any airline-to-airline comparison in this catalogue could show. This dataset does not score airlines on emissions, because the most recent independent per-airline fuel efficiency ranking, published by the International Council on Clean Transportation, dates to 2017 and could not be read directly to check before use; a stale number would be worse than none. Reviewed 2026-09. Suggest corrections through Contribute.

criteria.label: Flights within 15 minutes of schedule, arrivals and departures (UK CAA, 2025)

products.name: American Airlines
products.description: A full-service US network carrier flying domestic and international routes from hubs including Dallas-Fort Worth, Charlotte and Chicago O'Hare.

economical.note: American's own newsroom release says that for tickets bought on or after April 9, the first checked bag on domestic itineraries costs $45 prepaid online or $50 at the airport, and the second bag $55 prepaid or $60 at the airport; for Basic Economy tickets bought on or after May 18 the first bag costs $50 prepaid or $55 at the airport and the second $60 prepaid or $65 at the airport.

reliability.note: The UK Civil Aviation Authority's 2025 On Time Performance Tables (Top 50 airlines sheet, run 10 March 2026) record American Airlines flights at UK airports as within 15 minutes of schedule on 73.8 percent of flights, with an average delay of 22.3 minutes, across 16,116 total flights with arrivals and departures counted together.

cancellations.note: The same 2025 CAA table records American Airlines cancelling 2.78 percent of its 16,116 total flights.

products.name: Delta Air Lines
products.description: A full-service US network carrier with hubs including Atlanta, Detroit and Minneapolis-St Paul.

economical.note: Delta's own baggage overview page lists $45 USD for a first standard checked bag under 50 lbs, each way, and $55 USD for a second standard checked bag under 50 lbs, each way, for Delta Main and Delta Comfort customers.

reliability.note: The UK Civil Aviation Authority's 2025 On Time Performance Tables (Top 50 airlines sheet, run 10 March 2026) record Delta Air Lines flights at UK airports as within 15 minutes of schedule on 76.5 percent of flights, with an average delay of 15.3 minutes, across 8,669 total flights with arrivals and departures counted together.

cancellations.note: The same 2025 CAA table records Delta Air Lines cancelling 1.59 percent of its 8,669 total flights.

products.name: United Airlines
products.description: A full-service US network carrier with hubs including Chicago O'Hare, Denver, Houston and Newark.

economical.note: A news report on United's own fee change says the first checked bag on flights within the US, Mexico, Canada and Latin America now costs $45 and a second bag $55, a change United said followed roughly $400 million in added jet fuel costs since fighting began in the Middle East on February 28, 2026; co-branded credit card holders, certain loyalty-tier members, active-duty military and premium-cabin passengers still get a first bag free.

reliability.note: The UK Civil Aviation Authority's 2025 On Time Performance Tables (Top 50 airlines sheet, run 10 March 2026) record United Airlines flights at UK airports as within 15 minutes of schedule on 75.0 percent of flights, with an average delay of 18.1 minutes, across 15,659 total flights with arrivals and departures counted together.

cancellations.note: The same 2025 CAA table records United Airlines cancelling 1.88 percent of its 15,659 total flights.

products.name: Southwest Airlines
products.description: A US carrier historically built around low, simple point-to-point fares and open seating, sold mainly through its own site.

economical.note: CBS News reported that Southwest's first checked bag costs $35 and a second bag $45 starting May 28, 2025, ending the airline's long-standing free-checked-bag policy for most flyers; Business Select and A-List Preferred customers keep two free checked bags, and A-List members or Rapid Rewards credit card holders keep one.

products.description: A US carrier positioned between full-service and low-cost, based mainly at New York JFK and Boston.

economical.note: JetBlue's own fees page lists a first checked bag at $45 and a second at $59 for its Main Base fare, more than 24 hours before departure and outside peak periods; Main and EvenMore fares carry the same domestic checked-bag rates.

reliability.note: The UK Civil Aviation Authority's 2025 On Time Performance Tables (Top 50 airlines sheet, run 10 March 2026) record JetBlue Airways flights at UK airports as within 15 minutes of schedule on 82.6 percent of flights, with an average delay of 11.3 minutes, across 3,156 total flights with arrivals and departures counted together.

cancellations.note: The same 2025 CAA table records JetBlue Airways cancelling 0.73 percent of its 3,156 total flights.

products.name: easyJet
products.description: A UK-based airline flying short and medium-haul routes across Europe on an unbundled fare model.

economical.note: easyJet's own hold luggage page says each customer can add up to three hold bags in 15kg or 23kg sizes, that there is a charge for each hold item, and that adding bags online in advance is always cheaper than the £60 bag drop desk fee at the airport. The page shows no online price. Its site menu says the Business flexible fare includes one piece of hold luggage. The score rests on the published £60 desk fee and the per-bag charge.

reliability.note: The UK Civil Aviation Authority's 2025 On Time Performance Tables (Top 50 airlines sheet, run 10 March 2026) record easyJet Europe Group flights at UK airports as within 15 minutes of schedule on 72.5 percent of flights, with an average delay of 15.1 minutes, across 393,939 total flights with arrivals and departures counted together.
